item.description:
Nexa 1.0.13

  • Messages now look like other private Nostr messages: same format on the outside and much smaller (a short text is under 1 KB instead of about 3 KB), so relays can no longer pick out Nexa's messages so easily. The post-quantum keys now travel in small pieces, a bit in each message. This works once both of you have 1.0.13; chats with someone on an older version keep working as before.
  • With Tor, Nexa builds far fewer new circuits (about 60% fewer in busy chats), which looks more like a normal Tor user and is lighter on the Tor network.
  • If a message gets no delivery receipt within a few hours, Nexa sends it once more, in case a relay lost it.
  • Connections now look like Safari's, and message times are spread over two days, as other private Nostr messages are.

Also new since 1.0.11 (from 1.0.12)

  • Message headers and addresses now change along with the encryption keys. Someone who once copied a chat's keys from your Mac loses track of which messages belong to it within two replies, not just of what they say. This works once both of you have 1.0.12.
  • Group messages are now signed with a post-quantum signature (ML-DSA-65) as well, once everyone in the group has 1.0.12, so not even a quantum computer could fake who sent one. Existing groups switch at their next key change, and member codes change once; compare them again if you had. Group messages are now always padded to at least 8 KB.
  • The storage key is now kept out of swap and erased from memory as soon as Nexa locks.
  • Updates are safer: Nexa only installs one if the update list itself is signed with Nexa's update key, and checks the download before unpacking it.
